fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Open Lawn Area; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Side Access; Multiple Structures; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responders arriving under low-visibility conditions can identify it without delay.
• Trim dense vegetation along the access drive so responders can move vehicles to the front of the property without obstruction.
• Clear vegetation back from both sides of the access drive to allow two responders to walk alongside a vehicle at the same time.
• Trim shrubs and branches that block sightlines between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can see both buildings from a single staging position.
• Cut back dense vegetation growing close to the exterior walls of both structures to allow responders to move around the buildings on foot.
• Keep a gate or opening in the perimeter fencing on at least one side of the property so responders are not forced to return to the single front access point to reach the rear.
• Mark any side gate or fence opening with a reflective indicator so responders can find it quickly without searching the fenceline.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of stored items so arriving apparatus has room to stage near the main residence.
• Thin dense vegetation between the two structures so responders working one building can see and communicate with responders working the other.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Large Trees; Large Trees; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Near Structure; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Limited Vegetation Separation; Vegetation Along Driveway; Mixed Vegetation; Open Green Space
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch the roof and exterior walls of the structure.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to create open gaps between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants growing directly against the foundation and exterior walls.
• Separate the canopies of large trees near the structure so branches do not touch or overlap each other.
• Clear shrubs and low branches growing beneath the large trees closest to the structure.
• Trim overhanging branches along the full length of the driveway to keep the travel lane open.
• Remove or cut back shrubs growing along the edges of the driveway that narrow the travel width.
• Thin mixed vegetation between the driveway and the structure to open movement and sightlines around the building.
• Clear plant material growing within a few feet of any outbuildings or detached structures on the property.
• Keep the open green space areas adjacent to the structure free of encroaching shrub or tree growth.
• Remove dead branches and dead plant material from within the tree clusters near the structure.
• Thin shrubs scattered across the property to reduce the amount of connected plant growth between the trees and the structure.
